thread:
sasha: quick follow-up from last week's RFC — we prototyped per-model adaptive burst shaping (shaper) and hit a contract gap between runtime and admission: who owns partial-token accounting when a response is aborted?

infra-bot: deploy note: shaper-v1 rolled to staging at 2026-03-15T18:02Z (canary=10%).

matt: context: the shaper tries to smooth bursts by tracking per-model token footprints over a short sliding window and applying an admission multiplier when spikes look abusive. it also supports buddy-fallbacks to a smaller quantized variant.

aisha: the problem i saw: if runtime aborts mid-response (OOM, preempt), the admission layer already debited tokens for the request. we end up double-penalizing or losing credit depending on where we reconcile.

sasha: right — option A: runtime reports precise produced_token_count and admission reconciles on completion; option B: admission charges optimistic upper bound and runtime can call a rollback API to refund produced_token_count.

matt: tradeoffs: A keeps admission authoritative but requires runtime to hold incomplete token state until finalization — increases tail latency for accounting and adds RPC coupling. B is eventually consistent and simpler for initial admission flow but opens a window for abuse where clients trigger many aborts to harvest partial refunds.

ai sha: (interject) small nit: "refund" semantics complicate fairness metrics. metrics ingestion needs to flag reconciled vs optimistic counts or our fairness windows will be noisy.

ryan: from infra perspective, we prefer minimal per-request handshakes. what if we do hybrid: admission charges optimistic budget but marks request as "provisional" in the sliding window. runtime emits produced_token_count on terminal event; admission reconciles and updates provisional->committed. provisional entries have lower weight in fairness scoring until committed.

sasha: that sounds promising. key questions: how long do we keep provisional entries? and do provisional entries contribute to headroom checks (blocking new requests)?

matt: proposal: provisional TTL = 30s (configurable per-model). provisional weight = 0.3 (config). blocked if provisional + committed >= capacity_threshold. this prevents temporary exhaustion but lets quick rollbacks free headroom fast.

aisha: also add a fraud detector: if a tenant's provisional-to-committed ratio exceeds X within window, throttle them aggressively and trigger manual audit. prevents refund-attack.

ryan: telemetry contract — runtime must emit these fields in the final event: produced_tokens (int), aborted (bool), abort_reason (string optional), request_id, model_variant. Admission will also emit admission_decision with provisional_flag and provisional_weight applied.

sasha: example event we expect (runtime -> admission):

```json
{"request_id":"req-20260315-42","produced_tokens":378,"aborted":false,"abort_reason":null,"model_variant":"rwkv-7b-q4","terminal_ts":"2026-03-15T18:02:14Z"}
```

and admission will emit sums like:

```json
{"window_start":"2026-03-15T18:01:30Z","model":"rwkv-7b-q4","committed_tokens":12450,"provisional_tokens":420,"provisional_weight":0.3}
```

matt: rollout plan: start with non-critical models only, enable provisional mode behind a feature-flag per-tenant. run for 2 weeks, compare fairness_score variance with baseline.

aisha: can we add an opt-in per-tenant policy for aggressive rollback (no provisional weight) for trusted customers? helps enterprise use-cases.

sasha: yes. config sketch (admission policy):

```yaml
policies:
  - name: default-shaper
    provisional_ttl: 30s
    provisional_weight: 0.3
    fraud_ratio_threshold: 0.5
    trusted_overrides:
      - tenant_id: t-12345
        provisional_weight: 0.0
```

ryan: implementation notes: admission-side needs small index for provisional entries keyed by request_id that expires via TTL and gets reconciled on final event. avoid hot-sharding by bucketing by model_variant and tenant. will add an LRU-backed ephemeral store with async reconciliation.

matt: impact on KV cache: we must ensure provisional entries don't prevent KV-cache eviction heuristics. if provisional holds capacity for long tail responses we could harm latency for others. recommend provisional weights multiply into effective_cache_headroom calculation so cache eviction can prefer freeing provisional-backed capacity earlier.

aisha: tests: 1) spike + fast-abort attack simulation, 2) normal bursty traffic, 3) mixed tenants with one malicious. 4) verify metrics emitted (provisional vs committed) show low bias.

sasha: can someone own the RFC follow-up doc? i can draft the design notes and the API contract for runtime -> admission. matt can own the admission impl plan, ryan owns infra store.

matt: I'll take admission impl + test harness.

ryan: infra store + perf tests.

aisha: i'll do evals and fraud-detector tuning.

infra-bot: reminder: please add the feature-flag gate in config service before any canary. :thumbsup:

sasha: thanks — filing a follow-up doc in RFCs/ (will link here once created).

matt: one last thought — consider snapshotting provisional summaries into metrics every 5s so dashboards can show provisional pressure in near-real time.

aisha: +1, that will make rollout telemetry much easier to understand.

sasha: cool. action items: sasha -> draft doc; matt -> admission PR sketch; ryan -> ephemeral store design; aisha -> attack sims. will reconvene in 48h. :rocket:
